doc.title: Byron Stripling interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Opening and the word 'black' on tape
summary: Rowe opens the filming at Hamilton College; Stripling and Rowe joke about saying 'black' versus African American.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and we’re filming on the campus of Hamilton College today for the Jazz Archive. I’m very pleased to have Byron Stripling with me today, who has put some great time in at a jazz festival here, trumpeter, vocalist, actor, motivator. As a young man were you one of those people who liked to get up on the stage? Was that something that seemed to be part of your character even at a young age?
Not necessarily, but I think in all of our lives things happen and they sort of lead to something else, for me and I think for a lot of black people. Is it okay to say black on the tape?
Or do I have to say African American? I still say black, I haven’t shifted yet, you know.
I think we’re back to black actually.
We’re definitely not Afro-American. That’s supposed to be —
African-American. I mean I understand why the term is but I’ve got to just change my habit and it’s a longer word to say, so I just still say black.
I’ll say black if you say black, all right?
